title: Miami star WR Malachi Toney 'really close' to returning from ankle injury, Mario Cristobal says - CBS Sports
description: The Hurricanes may get their All-American playmaker back very soon before the College Football Playoff
body:
The Hurricanes may get their All-American playmaker back very soon before the College Football Playoff
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 20, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:07 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Miami might be getting standout wide receiver Malachi Toney back to its lineup earlier than expected, coach Mario Cristobal revealed Friday on "The Pat McAfee Show." The All-American candidate, who missed the Hurricanes' loss at Notre Dame and their 36-25 win over Duke after ankle surgery earlier this month, is "really close," according to Cristobal.Initial best-case estimates suggested Miami was preparing to have Toney back for its postseason run, but now the ACC's top playmaker could return for the conference title game if the Hurricanes secure a berth this weekend against Virginia Tech."I think the best part about it is that he is being very proactive about not being a distraction," Cristobal said. "He knows he's not playing right now, and he's gotta coach and encourage and push his teammates to be their very best while he gets prepared to play."Before his injury, Toney recorded 73 receptions for 1,027 yards and 13 touchdowns to lead the conference and was on pace to eclipse last season's record-setting numbers set as a true freshman.
Toney hurt his ankle in practice a few days before Miami's only loss of the season against the Fighting Irish."Obviously, losing a guy like Malachi hurts, but especially during the week, mid-game plan hurts even more," Miami wideout Cooper Barkate said after his team's win over Duke. "So, yeah, I think it was a little bit a little better coming into this week, knowing what we had and planning for success."Without Toney in the lineup, Shannon Dawson has been forced to scale back Miami's downfield passing game a bit in the last two games. Per 247Sports, Mensah is coming off a performance against Duke in which he threw for 382 yards and one touchdown with an average depth of target of 5.2 yards.
ACC defenses are going man against the Hurricanes, forcing other options behind Toney to try and beat them in single coverage. Despite not having the Heisman contender in the lineup, Miami owns college football's top-ranked scoring offense (averaging 44.1 points per game), ranks fourth in yards per game (518.1) and second in yards per play (7.42). Dawson said he sees the fans' frustrations on social media, angered by the Hurricanes' lack of explosion in the passing game without the sophomore."You have to be patient when defenses are playing a certain way," Dawson said. "I would love to throw a 70-yard touchdown every play. Is that realistic? I mean, some of our fans obviously think so, but the reality is [the defenses] have a say in the matter. If they're going to play a certain way, I can throw vertical every time if we want to go three-and-out. That's the easy way for me to get fired. That's exactly what they want — some of them."
Miami initially dropped six spots in the CFP Rankings from its top spot after its loss to Notre Dame. CFP chair Hunter Yurachek has said in each of the last two weeks after the reveal that the selection committee still "likes" the Hurricanes, who have "a lot of talent on that team with or without Malachi Toney."

title: Texas A&M expected to bench Marcel Reed: Aggies set to make QB change for Week 12 showdown vs. Oklahoma - CBS Sports
description: With Reed struggling mightily in 2026, Texas A&M is likely turning over the reins to Brady Hart for the clash wit
body:
With Reed struggling mightily in 2026, Texas A&M is likely turning over the reins to Brady Hart for the clash with the Sooners
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                            
        
    Nov 20, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:32 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Brady Hart is currently expected to get his first career start for Texas A&M on Saturday against Oklahoma, sources confirmed to CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz and Chris Hummer. The anticipated move comes after multi-year starter Marcel Reed struggled in last week's 22-7 loss vs. Tennessee, finishing 9-of-22 passing for 71 yards and an interception.A sophomore out of Cocoa Beach, Florida, Hart is 14 of 25 for 165 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions across appearances in four games. He threw both interceptions against LSU and Tennessee.Hart came into the game with 2:44 left at Kyle Field against Tennessee and received a roaring ovation after completing his first pass attempt for a first down to Mario Craver.Hart signed with Texas A&M in December 2024 after flipping his commitment from Michigan and reclassifying from the 2026 class to the previous cycle. Texas A&M pursued Hart after Husan Longstreet flipped his pledge from the Aggies to USC.
Texas A&M ranks 13th in the SEC in total offense, scoring offense, explosive plays and 15th in passing offense. Only Arch Manning and Sam Leavitt have thrown more interceptions than Reed, who's had two fewer attempts than the Texas quarterback and 53 fewer than LSU's starter.The Aggies chose to retain Reed this offseason after the dual-threat quarterback helped Texas A&M reach the College Football Playoff last fall for the first time in program history, despite struggling down the stretch. This season, the offense never got off the ground with Reed in charge under first-year OC Holmon Wiggins, who Mike Elko promoted this offseason from his previous stint as wide receivers coach.Hart might be the spark that Texas A&M (4-6) needs to reach bowl eligibility. The Aggies must beat the Sooners this weekend and upset Texas in Week 13 to get to the necessary six-win threshold.
CBS Sports reported earlier this week that the Aggies and Reed would likely part ways this offseason as both parties look to start fresh in 2027. If Reed heads to the bench against Oklahoma as expected, his season concludes with below-average numbers — 1,172 yards passing, eight touchdowns, nine interceptions and a completion rate of 55.7%.After rushing for six touchdowns and nearly 500 yards as a junior, Reed has just 206 yards and three scores this fall."Our offense is inept," Elko said after last week's performance against Tennessee. "I don't know how you can put this on one kid. It's on me. It's a completely nonfunctional offense. Come after me."
Elko called the team's offensive production pathetic following its sixth loss this season, but has not placed Reed under the microscope ... until now. Throwing Hart to the wolves against the Sooners means matching up with the SEC's fifth-best defense (294.6 yards per game).

title: Jerry Jones calls Cowboys 'a bad team'; says team has chance to play better after Christian Parker's demotion - CBS Sports
description: Jones feels Dallas is a bad team right now, but he defended the puzzling decision to demote Parker and keep him o
body:
Jones feels Dallas is a bad team right now, but he defended the puzzling decision to demote Parker and keep him on staff
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 20, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:05 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Eight teams have scored 26 or more points per game in the 2026 NFL season. The Buffalo Bills (31.9), the San Francisco 49ers (31.2), the Cincinnati Bengals (30.9), the Jacksonville Jaguars (29.9), the Dallas Cowboys (28.6), the Detroit Lions (28.6), the Chicago Bears (26.8), and the Kansas City Chiefs (26.3).The Cowboys are the only team among those eight with more than two losses, and they have a 4-6 record. Dallas is one of only two teams with a scoring defense below league average, and theirs ranks 30th (28.2 points per game) out of the league's 32 teams. That's why Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones felt comfortably calling his squad "a bad team" on Friday. "We have not been a good team and are a bad team," Jones said Friday on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas, via Yahoo Sports. "At 4-6, that says everything you need to say. ... Does that mean we will play a bad game [and] be a bad team on Sunday? Not necessarily. And that's why we're trying to improve."  One way the Cowboys tried to improve their ailing defense this week was to strip first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker of his play-calling duties and give them to senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine. However, Parker will stay on with the team to run defensive meetings and build out the game plans, but the 34-year-old, the youngest defensive coordinator in Cowboys history, will not have the play-calling role defensive coordinators usually have on game day. 
"We've got a chance to play better doing it this way," Jones said of Dallas' demotion of Parker, via The Dallas Morning News.   After Dallas allowed the 49ers to rack up 584 total yards, the most allowed in a Cowboys' home game in the 67-season history of the franchise, they now have the NFL's worst total defense (393.8 total yards per game allowed), run defense (154.1 rushing yards per game allowed), third down defense (48.8% third down conversion rate allowed) and the worst defense in terms of defensive expected points added (EPA) per play (-0.13).  Dallas Cowboys defense 2026 season, NFL ranksNFL rankPPG allowed28.230thTotal YPG allowed393.8LastRush YPG allowed154.1LastPass YPG allowed239.727thThird down conversion rate allowed48.8%LastCompletion percentage allowed66.7%27thTD-INT allowed19-428thPasser rating allowed104.529thEPA per play allowed-0.13LastTo be fair to Dallas' coaching staff, many of the defensive issues the last few years have been with the players on the field. Per CBS Sports Research, the Cowboys are the only team in NFL history to allow 27-plus points per game in three consecutive seasons with a different defensive coordinator each year: Mike Zimmer (2024), Matt Eberflus (2025) and now Parker (2026). Nothing has stuck, which likely has more to do with Jones' roster-building and decision to trade away All-Pro edge rusher Micah Parsons to the Green Bay Packers. 
Jones' and head coach Brian Schottenheimer's handling of Parker is very weird, but the move could at least get Dallas to a 6-6 record after Thanksgiving. Dallas hosts the 1-8 Tennessee Titans in Week 11, then takes on the 2-7 Philadelphia Eagles on Thanksgiving Day.

title: LSU women's basketball star MiLaysia Fulwiley has felony charges dropped in evading police case - CBS Sports
description: Fulwiley is still facing three misdemeanors stemming from an incident after an LSU football game
body:
Fulwiley is still facing three misdemeanors stemming from an incident after an LSU football game
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 20, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:46 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        LSU guard MiLaysia Fulwiley was arrested last Saturday and charged with five counts following an incident with a police officer who was directing traffic after an LSU football game in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. Fulwiley, accused of striking a police officer in a car and fleeing the scene, took to social media to deny the allegations before quickly deleting those posts.The two most serious charges against Fulwiley -- aggravated battery with a dangerous weapon and aggravated assault with a dangerous weapon -- were dropped by District Attorney Hillar Moore on Friday, per WAFB. Both charges were felonies. 
        
            
                LSU guard MiLaysia Fulwiley not with team in first game since arrest, Kim Mulkey stays quiet about status
                
                    Jack Maloney                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Her other three charges -- flight from an officer, resisting an officer and disobedience to police officers -- are all misdemeanors and remain for now. However, Moore said that they will be dismissed if she completes a pretrial diversion program. Fulwiley released a statement on Friday apologizing for her actions and social media posts.
"Saturday night ended in a situation that never should have happened, and my posts afterward made it worse. For that, I owe an apology to the officers involved and everyone who calls themselves a Tiger. I also want to apologize to my family and all those who love and support me," she said."People see the purple and gold before they see me, and I want to carry myself in a way that's worthy of it, on the court and off. Rules and laws apply to everyone, including the instructions of officers working a game night in Baton Rouge. I respect the job those officers do, and I'll let the legal process run its course. My focus is doing what this program asks of me and earning back the trust of the people who count on me."Fulwiley was not with LSU for its two games this week, and coach Kim Mulkey declined to comment on her status. LSU social media accounts did not acknowledge Fulwiley's inclusion on the John Wooden Award Top 50 Watch List this week.Fulwiley played her freshman and sophomore seasons at South Carolina before transferring to LSU. She has won back-to-back SEC Sixth Player of the Year awards and is currently projected as a top 10 pick in the 2027 WNBA Draft. 
Through her first four games this season, Fulwiley is averaging 17.8 points, 3.5 rebounds, 4.3 assists, 4.3 steals and 2.8 blocks on 54.9% shooting. LSU is off to a 6-0 start and is ranked No. 9 in the country.

title: UFC Fight Night: Navajo Stirling risks dilemma with teammate, champ Carlos Ulberg - CBS Sports
description: Stirling could catapult himself into the 205-pound title picture with a win over former champ Jiri Prochazka in Q
body:
Stirling could catapult himself into the 205-pound title picture with a win over former champ Jiri Prochazka in Qatar this weekend

        Navajo Stirling is days away from the biggest fight of his career, but victory could create an uncomfortable situation. Stirling fights former UFC light heavyweight champion Jiri Prochazka in Saturday's UFC Fight Night main event in Qatar. Beating Prochazka would be a cause for celebration, though it comes with awkward baggage.A victory would put Stirling on the shortlist of contenders worthy of challenging for the UFC light heavyweight championship. Unfortunately, the title belongs to Stirling's close friend and teammate, Carlos Ulberg. It's an uncomfortable reality that Stirling seems reluctant to stew on."Obviously, it's quite confrontational and all of that," Stirling told CBS Sports. "It's just one of the things where I don't want to think about it. I want to just focus on the fight that's in front of me. That's Jiri."Sign up for Paramount+ and watch UFC Fight Night in Qatar for no additional fee -- every UFC numbered event and UFC Fight Night is included with your subscription! Plans start as low as $8.99/month or $89.99/year!
Stirling has a point. A potential fight with Ulberg is irrelevant if he can't get past Prochazka. The possibility hasn't driven a wedge between the teammates, either. Far from it. Ulberg has been incredibly supportive of Stirling, encouraging him to do to Prochazka what Ulberg did in April."I've talked to Carlos; he wants nothing more than for me to remind him that the Kiwis down under are just as good," Stirling said. "I'm looking to do a job on him and absolutely put him out and have him go zero and two against the Kiwis. So I think that's what I'm looking to do."
Stirling's tone towards potentially fighting Ulberg has shifted throughout 2026. In July, he said he had no interest in challenging his teammate, preferring to wait and support Ulberg as he established himself as champion.
"My time will come; there's no rush," Stirling told Australian publication nine.com.au. "I'm sure when that title slot opens up, I'll be able to slide right in comfortably. We don't really think about it that much. "I know my relationship with the boys is sweet, I've got no animosity, and my ambitions don't trump theirs and vice versa."Three months later, Stirling was less definitive. In an October interview with New Zealand sports podcast Sports Fix, he suggested the decision wasn't his alone. It would depend on UFC matchmakers and City Kickboxing head coach Eugene Bareman.
"We'll just see what the UFC wants to do, what the coach wants to do, because we're from the same gym," Stirling said. "So, yeah, it's not up to me. It's up to Eugene and the team at CKB."
        
            
                UFC Fight Night predictions -- Jiri Prochazka vs. Navajo Stirling: Fight card, odds and expert picks in Qatar
                
                    Shakiel Mahjouri                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Stirling is partially right. No fight happens without the UFC offering it, and Bareman has considerable influence as the shepherd of New Zealand's premier MMA gym. Ultimately, though, there's no fight unless Stirling and Ulberg agree to it."My team is all behind me," Stirling said ahead of Saturday's fight with Prochazka. "We're just leaving all of that stuff till later."
The 29-year-old contender is taking a mature approach. UFC championships have irreparably damaged friendships before, most notably between T.J. Dillashaw and Cody Garbrandt, and Jon Jones and Rashad Evans. City Kickboxing has avoided similar public fallout, a credit to Bareman's leadership. The gym also handled former middleweight champion Israel Adesanya's exit with grace.That camaraderie extends beyond one gym.Australia and New Zealand have become a unified front in MMA. Unlike the bitter rivalry between Florida-based gyms American Top Team and the Blackzilians from 2011 to 2017, fighters from the neighboring countries frequently cross-train and share knowledge. Australian lightweight contender Tom Nolan has expressed similar apprehension about potentially fighting fellow countryman Quillan Salkilld. Stirling believes the cooperation comes from decades of playing catch-up with the rest of the MMA world.
"I can tell you what it is," Stirling said. "We've been behind the rest of the world for so long, and we're a very small martial arts community Down Under and Aussie and New Zealand, compared to the rest of the world. We've been very limited in resources compared to most other big countries. We're not government-funded. It's all passion. Everyone knows that getting to where we are now takes a lot of effort."Because we've been so behind for so long, we've developed our skills to be way better than most of the rest of the world," Stirling said. "I think because we're such small, small nations, people still think that we're limited. Like we're not that good, but we are that good."Stirling intends to prove just that against Prochazka. A victory on Saturday would be his fourth this year and second against a former UFC champion, putting him firmly in the Breakout Fighter of the Year conversation and potentially earning consideration for Fighter of the Year.
And after watching Ulberg knock out Prochazka despite fighting with a torn ACL, Stirling likes his chances."I think one thing that he's struggling with is accepting that another man is better. He thinks it's something about him," Stirling said. "He's always coming up with some sort of excuse. We've heard it before. Dark magic. No mercy. I think we're just starting to realize it might be something to do with himself."We've seen his limits. Where he goes and where he falls short. I don't think there's a new version of him. And even if there is, I'll be very much prepared because we haven't seen my limits yet."

title: How Louisville City plans to tackle rare morning kickoff vs. Sacramento Republic in Saturday's USL final - CBS Sports
description: Staying on East Coast time is part of the strategy as the club chases its first league title since 2018 against a
body:
Staying on East Coast time is part of the strategy as the club chases its first league title since 2018 against a Sacramento squad riding a 16-game unbeaten streak
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 20, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:55 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        In recent years, Louisville City FC have been one of the most successful regular-season teams in United Soccer League history, but it hasn't translated to winning the big game. They haven't won the USL Championship since 2018, and while this season has been a trying time dealing with injuries and a new coach taking over, they're playing their best soccer when it matters to set up a strange clash with Sacramento Republic at noon Eastern on Saturday. What's strange isn't that it's Louisville and Sacramento meeting, but that the match kicks off at 9 a.m. local time, a time Louisville forward Ray Serrano says he hasn't played soccer at since he was 15. While it's a regular training time for Louisville and they'll try to keep things on an East Coast timeline, it's hard not to take the shift into account when planning for a final.It's a challenge that comes with the desire to reach as many fans as possible with a final of this magnitude. Leagues have to work with broadcast networks to ensure that the slots work, and for the USL, having the game on CBS is worth the risk of a 9 a.m. local start with a West Coast team hosting. It's nothing Louisville won't be prepared for, as they look to keep their internal clocks on Eastern Standard Time.How to watch Sacramento Republic vs. Louisville City FC, oddsDate: Saturday, Nov. 20 | Time: Noon ET (9 a.m. PT)Location: Heart Health Park -- Sacramento, CaliforniaTV: CBSOdds: Sacramento Republic +110; Draw +230; Louisville +240"No, we're trying to stay on Eastern Time, so for us, it's training time," defender Kyle Adams said. "Wake up at 8:00 a.m., but really it's 5:00 a.m. Go to sleep a little bit earlier. Try to do everything really just to stay on Eastern Time, eat a little bit earlier on the night before, and just treat it as going into training, and then get after them."Other teams have dealt with similar issues, like the Los Angeles Rams when playing an NFL game in Australia, but it's still a struggle to deal with en route to a cup final as Louisville look to reach the pinnacle of the sport for the first time since 2018. Winners of the Prinx Tires USL Cup during the regular season, they do have cup experience that will prove to be fruitful in this competition, which Adams noted has been something that brings the injury-riddled squad together. "We know in the last few years we've struggled in these knockout games, but this year we've turned it on," Serrano said. "It has been really good preparation, just the mentality of going into them, how we deal with the pressure, and we're seeing the fruits of all that now."It's cliche to say that because of the adversity that they've dealt with, the club is playing its best soccer when it matters, but between using four goalkeepers during the season and seeing manager Danny Cruz depart to be an assistant manager with Minnesota United, it hasn't been an easy task for interim manager Simon Bird to get this team on the right track at this critical juncture.
"Going back to the main part is the adversity that we've faced. You mentioned injuries, having to deal with that side of it, some of the various parts of the season, different things we've had to deal with from a tactical or technical standpoint, where we've lost games, and we feel that we shouldn't have lost games," Bird said when reflecting on the team's development under his leadership. "The most impressive thing I said to the guys today, yesterday in training, we worked on our defensive structure, but the whole training session I thought was excellent, not just the defensive side, off the ball but with the ball, and to see it all come together towards the end of the season is really rewarding. Hopefully, we can carry that on and put together a complete performance, and that's what we've had throughout the season-moments where we've let ourselves down in all these different areas, set pieces, maybe transition at other times, in front of goal. So, putting it all together for a complete performance on Saturday is the goal."Traveling away to a tough environment in Heart Health Park, Louisville will meet the hottest team in the league in Sacramento Republic. They've ridden a club-record 16-game unbeaten run to the final based on their defense. That has set a strong foundation to build on, and it could make the final one where the first team to score a goal wins the match. Sacramento's squad also has experience in USL Cup finals, which goes a long way when preparing for games of this stature."I don't think it can hurt to have that. This would be a step forward for my first final. I think experience is invaluable for players and for staff," Sacramento coach Neil Collins said. "But then there's also the recognition that every game is different, every team is different, and every season is different. So it's just trying to get the balance right and enjoy the opportunity. You've got to have the mechanisms to control the things you can control. Obviously, the opposition team is trying to do the same, and we've got to do everything we can to be ready to take the opportunity when it comes. But the experience will definitely help us; there's plenty of that in our dressing room."
It's a final where the best that the league has to offer will be on display, and it couldn't come at a better time. The summer of soccer, with the United States hosting the World Cup alongside Mexico and Canada, has truly turned into a soccer avalanche, and this final showcases one of the top atmospheres in the league. You can't ask for much better than that, as no matter what, a drought will come to an end. Sacramento Republic haven't won the final since 2014, while Louisville haven't won since 2018, and for these clubs, it will mean a lot to get back to the top.

title: Colts waive Daniel Jones: Indy not trading QB or Jonathan Taylor at deadline now a major second-guess - CBS Sports
description: Indy has put themselves in a very tough spot after sitting on the fence at the deadline.
body:
Indy has put themselves in a very tough spot after sitting on the fence at the deadline.
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 20, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:43 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Mobb Deep said it best: "Ain't no such thing as halfway crooks." The Indianapolis Colts tried to sit on the fence at the 2026 trade deadline, ship away some (not all) expendable pieces, and land a somewhat respectable, middle-of-the-road record that might save a few jobs in the process. That meant moving on from the likes of DeForest Buckner, Quenton Nelson, and Josh Downs, but holding on to Jonathan Taylor and Daniel Jones. Less than two weeks removed from that semi-fire sale, it's safe to say Indy botched it. What's the old saying? If you're going to be a bear, be a grizzly. Well, if the Colts felt alright selling some pieces at the deadline, they should've stripped it down to the studs, knowing full well they are entering a rebuild anyway after firing GM Chris Ballard in mid-October. The losses have only continued to pile up for the Colts, which includes a demoralizing defeat at the hands of the Houston Texans in Week 11. That game, which dropped them to 3-8, proved to be the straw that broke the camel's back for the Daniel Jones era, as the team has since waived the veteran quarterback. 
Again, this is a player who teams were reportedly interested in leading up to the deadline. Instead of pursuing those opportunities to shed a sunk-cost under center, ESPN reports that Indy rebuffed trade interest from teams like the Minnesota Vikings and Baltimore Ravens. 
As a reminder, the Vikings traded a 2027 third-round pick to acquire Kirk Cousins, while the Ravens shipped a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 seventh-round pick to the Cardinals in exchange for Jacoby Brissett and a 2027 fifth-round pick. It's unclear what the compensation for Jones would've been, but I can tell you this—it's more than what they have now after waiving him: nothing.  In the nine games before the deadline, Jones had the Colts at 2-7 while completing 60.3% of his passes, averaging just 191.3 passing yards per game, and posting a passer rating of 68.9. In total, Jones had tallied seven touchdowns and 13 turnovers. Daniel Jones prior to 2026 trade deadlineStatsTeam record2-7Completion percentage60.3%Passing YPG191.3Pass TDs6INTs10Yards per attempt5.7Air yards per attempt4.6Passer rating68.9Ruhsing YPG17.4Rushing TDs1Fumbles lost3It was abundantly clear in the lead-up to the deadline that the two-year, $88 million extension the Colts signed Jones this offseason to was a disaster. Miraculously, a lifeboat drifted by them in the form of multiple teams inquiring about taking that burden off their hands, but they decided to stay on the deserted island. Now they're paying the price, with Jones set to account for $35.2 million in dead cap space for 2027 (provided he clears waivers) while the team pays him $49.8 million for 11 games played this season. On top of Jones, Taylor, arguably the most sought-after prize on the trade market this cycle, should've been firmly on the block. With the Colts now without a clear answer at quarterback, Taylor is the living embodiment of that meme where the Lamborghini is sitting in the driveway of the trailer park. He was most valuable to Indy as a trade chip at the deadline, and that remains the case this offseason. The only difference is that any team acquiring him is getting a back that's a little older, has a little more mileage, and doesn't help them for this stretch run in 2026. That sets up a possibly diminished return this offseason if/when the Colts deal him compared to what they could've gotten at this deadline. For a team that won't have its first-round pick in 2027 after trading for Sauce Gardner at last year's deadline, they were in a position to refill the cupboard. Neither Jones nor Taylor likely would've fetched a first-rounder, but they would've given Indy premium ammunition for a later deal that could vault them back up. That level of asset mismanagement around the deadline now has the potential to ripple beyond just this second half of the season. Jones being waived is just one of the initial steps that the Colts will take as they embark on this rebuild and they tripped out of the gate. Whether it's firing Shane Steichen, trading Taylor, or eventually hiring a new GM (if they can find a taker), the organization needs to have a more definitive and realistic plan for its future so they're not looking back with major second guesses like they currently are following this deadline.

Hopefully we see more performances like that the rest of the weekend. Kenneth Walker ruled outThe Chiefs are huge favorites against the Cardinals and play the Bills on Thanksgiving, so it makes sense to give Walker another week. Emmett Johnson is once again a must-start running back and my number two running back overall in full PPR leagues. Brock Bowers was present at practice on ThursdayWe don't think this was a full practice, but it is fantastic news that he was there at all after leaving Week 10 with an ankle injury. We are projecting Bowers to play this week, which of course makes him a must-start tight end. You may want to pick up Michael Mayer just in case, as Mayer would be a borderline top 12 tight end if Bowers is ultimately unable to go.Baker Mayfield returned to practice on ThursdayMayfield missed Wednesday but got a limited session in on Thursday. While the vibe early in the week was negative, we're now prepared to project Mayfield as in on Sunday. That doesn't mean we want to start him. What it does mean is that Bucky Irving is a must-start RB1, and Emeka Egbuka is an upside WR3. Still, if you picked up Jalon Daniels in a Superflex league, you should hold him just in case.
DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks trending towards returnSmith and Wicks were both at practice on Wednesday and Smith sounds like someone who will play. If he does, he's the only Eagles wide receiver we want to start, and he'll be ranked as a WR2. If Smith needs one more week, then Makai Lemon is in play as a borderline WR2 in full PPR. Joe Milton is still expected to start at quarterback, so we won't get too excited about anyone in this passing game. For what it's worth, we like Dallas Goedert more without Smith than with him, but he's a top 12 tight end either way.Darren Waller and Tommy Tremble both questionableWaller and Tremble both got limited sessions in on Thursday and Friday. Since Week 8, Bryce Young has thrown 34.7% of his passes to tight ends, so either of these could be used in a pinch. We'll view Waller as a borderline top-12 tight end if he is active. If Waller is out, then Tremble is a high-end TE2. If either misses, it could be a boost to Jalen Coker, who has seen his target share shrink as the tight ends got more involved. Jonathon Brooks is also questionable, but we don't expect him to have a meaningful role even if he's active.Roman Wilson and Michael Pittman questionableThe biggest impact here is a big blow to Germie Bernard, who falls outside of the top 40 receivers. We are ranking Wilson as a low-end WR3 and DK Metcalf as a borderline WR2. If the Steelers have success running the ball against Philadelphia, it may turn out that you do not want to start any of the Steelers' pass catchers. We would like to see Pittman do something positive before we even think about putting him in our lineup.
Jordan Addison out, T.J. Hockenson and Jauan Jennings backAddison had surgery on his thumb. He won't go on IR, but he definitely won't play this week. That could make Jennings more interesting in a revenge game, but Jennings has shown nothing this year that would make you want to trust him. With Hockenson back, we will rank him as a top 12 tight end. This is a small boost for Kirk Cousins, who is a low-floor streamer.Geno Smith attempting to play, Omar Cooper and Isaiah Williams outI am not sure Smith will get in a full session this week but he has said he plans to play through his ankle injury. We don't really want to start him, but would much rather start Garrett Wilson and Breece Hall if he plays. Adonai Mitchell is also a good boom/bust WR3 assuming Smith plays. Mitchell gets a boost with the decrease. If Cade Klubnik has to start, we will downgrade the entire Jets offense.Jacory Croskey-Merritt practicing in fullWe are expecting Croskey-Merritt to return on Monday night but we have no idea how touches will be distributed between him, Rachaad White, and Austin Ekeler. Unless you are in a truly desperate situation, we would like to avoid all three. If you must, we are ranking them White, Crockey-Merritt, and Ekeler in that order. The first two are high-end flexes while Ekeler is only for the most desperate of managers.
Dalton Kincaid doubtfulThe tight end position looks even more like a disaster with Kincaid likely out. Dawson Knox could be a deep steamer at the position, but we don't have much faith in him, especially since the Bills are huge favorites and may not throw many passes. This could be a small boost in targets for Khalil Shakir, who is a low-end WR3.Josh Johnson preparing to start for Carson BeckThe Arizona Cardinals nightmare continues. While it is never a good thing to start your fourth different QB, I am not sure there will be a huge drop-off from what Beck was going to give us. You can be as nervous as you want about Trey McBride; there's no sitting him. We don't really want to start anyone else from this offense but Zonovan Knight is our favorite flex if you are absolutely desperate.Mike Evans trending towards questionableThe 49ers have a huge game this week against the Vikings, so it wouldn't be surprising if Evans pushes to play. How much he plays is another question altogether. I think the safest way to view Evans is as an upside WR3 if he gives it ago. We would be much less interested in starting Keenan Allen and Deebo Samuel if Evans returns. What's worse is this is a Sunday night game, so you'll need a backup plan if you are waiting out any of these guys.
Ladd McConkey limitedMcConkey has a chance to play this week but we aren't sure if we want him to. He's been terribly frustrating for Fantasy managers and will probably rank as an upside WR3 if he's active. Tre Harris is a Wr3 without McConkey but we would have a hard time starting him if the team's WR1 returns.

title: Royce Lewis trade grades: Dodgers land former No. 1 pick; Twins get another arm, arrow-up prospect - CBS Sports
description: Minnesota added right-hander Bobby Miller and catching prospect Francisco Espinoza in return
body:
Minnesota added right-hander Bobby Miller and catching prospect Francisco Espinoza in return
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 20, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:10 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Los Angeles Dodgers have added a former No. 1 overall pick. The Dodgers are set to acquire infielder Royce Lewis from the Minnesota Twins for right-hander Bobby Miller and minor-league catcher Francisco Espinoza, reports the New York Post. Neither team has announced the trade.Lewis, 27, was a candidate to be non-tendered prior to Friday's deadline. Rather than cut him loose, the Twins were able to find a trade partner and receive something in return. The No. 1 pick in the 2017 draft has battled injuries throughout his career and posted a .288 on-base percentage the last three years. Lewis simply failed to launch with Minnesota.
The Dodgers figure to use Lewis as a platoon partner for Max Muncy at third base and could also move him around the infield as a utility guy. The Twins moved him from third base to first base this past season. Lewis has played every infield position in the big leagues, though he's had only one inning at shortstop since 2022.Miller, 27, has been unable to build on his dynamic 2022 rookie season, when he threw 124 ⅓ innings with a 3.76 ERA. He has battled injuries and control issues since then, and the Dodgers moved him into the bullpen this past season. Miller has a 7.75 ERA in 134 ⅔ Triple-A innings the last three years and can be optioned down in 2027.
Espinoza, 19, reached Low Class-A in 2026 and hit .317/.411/.422 with three home runs and strong contact rates in 46 games. He does not rank among the top 30 Dodgers prospects at Baseball America or MLB Pipeline, but Espinoza is an arrow-up prospect and a solid return for a non-tender candidate.Here now are our grades for the two-for-one trade.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Los Angeles Dodgers: AAt worst, Lewis will be a high-priced utility guy next season. He's projected to make $5 million or so through arbitration and that simply is not much for the Dodgers, who have a history of getting underperforming hitters to the next level (like Muncy). At best, Lewis could be the new Chris Taylor and reach his offensive ceiling while bouncing between positions.Espinoza is a good prospect, not a great prospect, and Miller is a reclamation project. Those are easy players for the Dodgers to surrender to take a chance on Lewis and his upside. It may not work. Lewis could continue to get hurt and not hit, but it was a low-cost move and the chance of a reward is significant. 
It's a very nice upside play for a team that has hit on a lot of upside plays over the year.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Minnesota Twins: AIt's a bummer things didn't work out for Lewis and the Twins, but the reality is he was a non-tender candidate, and it wasn't a secret. Minnesota was able to get back a solid prospect in Espinoza and a lottery ticket arm in Miller despite having little leverage. Getting two players for Lewis is a very good outcome under the circumstances.
Giving each team an "A" suggests a win-win, and maybe it will be. There's a chance it's a lose-lose, though. Lewis may not hit, Miller may never rediscover his 2022 form, and Espinoza may not pan out. I see the vision for both teams, though and like it. 
The Dodgers rolled the dice on a talented player and the Twins were able to fetch two players for someone they might have otherwise cut loose and sent into free agency.

title: What's next for the Twins? Three things Minnesota must do to make a postseason push in 2027 season - CBS Sports
description: Minnesota has already signed Sonny Gray and brought back Ryan Jeffers, but there's more to be done
body:
Minnesota has already signed Sonny Gray and brought back Ryan Jeffers, but there's more to be done
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 20, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:55 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        It has been a surprisingly productive week for the Minnesota Twins. First, catcher Ryan Jeffers accepted the $23.15 million qualifying offer on Tuesday. Jeffers turned down a multi-year offer from the Twins, according to The Athletic, so he's betting on himself. Betting that he'll at least maintain his free agent stock and get paid next offseason.   Then, on Wednesday, the Twins brought back veteran righty Sonny Gray with a two-year contract worth $55 million. There's an opt-out after the first year. Gray, 37, finished fifth in the AL Cy Young voting this season and pitched wonderfully for the Twins in 2022 and 2023. He joins a rotation that, on paper, looks like one of the better starting units in the American League.Here is Minnesota's rotation depth chart:RHP Sonny GrayRHP Joe RyanRHP Pablo López (coming back from Tommy John surgery)RHP Taj BradleyRHP Dean KremerRHP Bailey OberRHP Zebby MatthewsLHP Connor PrielippRHP Mick AbelRHP David Festa (coming back from shoulder and thoracic outlet surgery)"I really don't take it lightly that he chose us," GM Jeremy Zoll told the Associated Press about Gray's return. "He had an abundance of options, and given where he's at in his career, I know how important it is to him. He expressed it quite directly how important it is to win, and this isn't just about having a good season or a winning season. It's about winning and going deep in the playoffs and making a real playoff run."    Matthews could land in the bullpen next season and that might be his long-term home. His stuff should be well suited to a relief role. Gray makes the rotation better and potentially the bullpen better as well by bumping Matthews to relief. Jeffers accepting the qualifying offer keeps a key middle-of-the-order bat in place. A good week for the Twins, this has been.   
After a disappointing 77-85 finish this year, Minnesota has already improved significantly in the early days of the offseason. They play in the AL Central. With all due respect, it is not the most imposing division. There's no reason the Twins can't be in the division and wild card races next season. Here now is what's left on Minnesota's offseason to-do list.   1. Sort out their non-tenders   Teams had until 5 p.m. ET Friday to offer their pre-arbitration and arbitration-eligible players contracts for 2027. They didn't have to sign them Friday, but they had to tender an offer; otherwise, the player immediately became a free agent. Dozens of players were cut loose at the non-tender deadline, as usual, and two players stood out as non-tender candidates for the Twins: Trevor Larnach and Royce Lewis. Larnach was indeed non-tendered, while Lewis was dealt to the Dodgers. OF Trevor Larnach
It's not often a player gets non-tendered after posting a .352 on-base percentage and 120 OPS+, but the writing was on the wall. The Twins had an agreement in place to trade Larnach at the deadline (Astros owner Jim Crane nixed the deal) and they have a very crowded outfield. Also, Larnach had wrist surgery earlier this month. That created some questions going into next season, and the Twins opted to cut him loose. 
Larnach had one more year of control remaining and was expected to make over $6 million through arbitration in 2027. I reckon the Twins tried again to trade him prior to Friday's non-tender deadline. In the end, he was non-tendered rather than risk tying $6 million or so up in yet another outfielder, particularly one who is coming off wrist surgery.   1B Royce Lewis 
Things got so bad this summer that Lewis, who has a .288 on-base percentage in over 1,200 plate appearances the last three years, was sent to Triple-A for a spell, and also moved across the diamond from third base to first base. The Twins could not count on him to provide offense and now he's playing a position with a high offensive bar. That made him expendable. Lewis, 27, was under team control through 2028 and that extra year was an important consideration for the club. His salary would have been in the $5 million range next season through arbitration, which is pricey but not exorbitant. Now, Lewis will receive a fresh start with the Dodgers, where he can be one of the guys, not the former No. 1 overall pick and expected face of the franchise.   
The Twins presumably did not want to give up on a player with as much talent as Lewis. At the same time, they kept trying, and it never worked. 2. Fill out the bullpen   
The Twins got a head start on their offseason bullpen shopping when they acquired Jeff Hoffman at the trade deadline. He has one more year remaining on the contract and will be in the team's late-inning mix in 2027. Here is manager Derek Shelton's bullpen unit at the moment:   Closer: RHP Yoendrys GómezSetup: RHP Jeff Hoffman and LHP Andrew MorrisMiddle: LHP Kody Funderburk and RHP Tommy NanceLong: RHP Travis Adams and LHP Kendry Rojas  Depth: RHP Marco Raya and RHP Cole SandsMorris is not yet a household name, but he has a great arm and was dominant at times in 2026. The Twins have themselves a nice little late-inning trio in Gómez, Hoffman, and Morris. A spare starter like Matthews or Prielipp could wind up in the bullpen as well. Given the quality of their stuff, they have a chance to make a real impact as relievers.   
Clearly though, the middle relief could use some help, and the Twins wouldn't need to spend big dollars to improve it. A second-tier free agent like, say, Andrew Kittredge would be a solid pickup. It's worth giving the Miami Marlins a call to see what it would take to get Anthony Bender and/or Michael Petersen. Point is, the bullpen can be improved, for sure.   3. Settle on an outfield groupThe Twins have way more outfielders than outfield spots and that is in no way a bad thing. First and foremost, it allows them to use Byron Buxton as the full-time DH, which could help keep him on the field. Secondly, there's no such thing as too many good players. Depth is important and the Twins certainly have plenty of it in the outfield.   More outfielders than outfield spots is not a problem. It's just something the Twins have to figure out. Even if we assume Buxton will DH and is not part of the outfield mix, here are the outfielders Minnesota must sort through:   
Incumbent MLB players: Trevor Larnach and Luke KeaschallMLB-ready top prospects: Walker Jenkins and Emmanuel RodriguezLefty-hitting Triple-A guys: Hendry Mendez and Alan RodenRighty-hitting utility guys: Ryan Kreidler and Austin MartinRodriguez is one of the game's 50 or so best prospects and he is out of minor league options, meaning he must go through waivers to go to Triple-A. Obviously, the Twins won't waive him. Non-tendering Larnach allows the Twins to play Rodriguez alongside Jenkins and Keaschall in the outfield, keep Kreidler and Martin on the bench, and keep the others in Triple-A.

title: Aljamain Sterling says critics can argue with the history books as he chases more legacy: 'Numbers don't lie' - CBS Sports
description: Sterling believes a win over Kevin Vallejos at UFC Fight Night in Qatar could put him in line for a second title
body:
Sterling believes a win over Kevin Vallejos at UFC Fight Night in Qatar could put him in line for a second title shot in as many divisions
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 20, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:30 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        LAS VEGAS -- A UFC title run didn't earn Aljamain Sterling the respect it should've. Fans haven't warmly embraced him or his many accomplishments as one of the best bantamweights ever. But the "Funk Master" is stubborn and talented enough to try and achieve something that even his boldest cynics would have trouble disputing.Sterling fights Kevin Vallejos in Saturday's UFC Fight Night co-main event in Qatar. A victory could put the former bantamweight champion in line to challenge Alexander Volkanovski for the featherweight title, giving Sterling a chance to join the exclusive club of UFC fighters who have won two weight class titles. It's an opportunity the No. 4-ranked featherweight contender never expected to have this late in his career.Sterling has already accomplished more than enough to retire comfortably. He holds UFC bantamweight records for most consecutive wins and title defenses. Yet the chance to add another championship to his resume has kept him sharp. He knows better than most that winning a title doesn't always win over critics, but the numbers on his side are irrefutable."I think it's just the history books," Sterling told CBS Sports. "I have enough money where I'm more than comfortable. More money is always good, though. But I think it's just the history. That's really it. Just setting records, doing something that no one could ever take away from you."
Sign up for Paramount+ and watch UFC Fight Night in Qatar for no additional fee -- every UFC numbered event and UFC Fight Night is included with your subscription! Plans start as low as $8.99/month or $89.99/year!Sterling has obsessed over accolades since his amateur wrestling days, when he never achieved the championship success he wanted. That disappointment fueled his MMA career, eventually carrying him to the UFC bantamweight title and three successful defenses. Moving up to featherweight allowed him to repeat that cycle all over again."I came up short in my amateur wrestling career; I never won a national title, never got to go to the state tournament, and it just always made me hungrier to keep pushing," Sterling said. "I became a UFC champ, and after setting the records, I came up short in my last one. Then I went up to 45, and now here's a new goal. I could become a two-division champion. I think that's a special feat in itself. People can talk and say whatever they want, but numbers don't lie. So for me, that's what it's all about."
Sterling's relationship with UFC fans has been complicated since he first won the bantamweight title in 2021. Petr Yan handed him the championship after striking him with a blatantly illegal knee, resulting in a disqualification. Sterling was accused of exaggerating the damage to win a title in a fight he was clearly losing. The stink lingered even after the "Funk Master" defeated Yan in their rematch and successfully defended the championship against T.J. Dillashaw and Henry Cejudo.His reign ended just as frustratingly. Sterling faced Sean O'Malley on a quick turnaround despite dealing with injuries, losing by second-round TKO. He then moved to featherweight without a red-carpet rollout for his 135-pound accomplishments. Sterling isn't deaf to the accusations that he isn't as good as his record suggests, despite repeatedly beating fighters whom his critics hold in high regard."People still want to find a way to chip away at what I've done. Dude, look at the numbers. Clearly, I'm better than what you think," Sterling said. "I can't be that bad if I'm beating all these other guys that you rate at this level. It is what it is. I'm comfortable in my own skin. I know I've done enough. And again, for me, numbers don't lie. So if you want to say this or that, I go, 'OK, but what does it say in the history books?' So go argue with the numbers, don't argue with me."

        
            
                UFC Fight Night predictions -- Jiri Prochazka vs. Navajo Stirling: Fight card, odds and expert picks in Qatar
                
                    Shakiel Mahjouri                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Some fans made up their minds about Sterling the night Yan threw that illegal knee. No amount of winning will change their minds about his alleged Oscar-worthy dive. But becoming a two-division UFC champion by beating Volkanovski would make Sterling's place in MMA history much harder to dispute. He would have achieved something that many champions, including Volkanovski, never managed.Not everyone is blind to Sterling's abilities, especially those who've competed at the highest level of MMA. Volkanovski has publicly identified Sterling as the featherweight contender most deserving of a title shot, provided he beats Vallejos. It's a meaningful endorsement, given the interest in knockout artist Jean Silva as the next challenger. Recent title challenger Movsar Evloev, who narrowly defeated Sterling in December 2024, has also vouched for his former opponent. Evloev previously told CBS Sports that Silva wouldn't sniff a title shot if he had to beat Sterling first. The praise from his peers means more than criticism from those who have never set foot inside the Octagon.
"I've trained with Volk. I fought Movsar. So these guys know what they're looking at," Sterling said. "They know what they understand, see and can feel. It lets me know I'm doing something right. I'm just very fortunate, very blessed to be in this situation still."MMA suffers from short-term memory. Even Charles Oliveira and Max Holloway, beloved former champions who built legacies off thrilling performances, encountered persistent criticism after their underwhelming BMF title fight earlier this year. In team sports, many fans have an attitude of "What have you done for me lately?" It's becoming more prevalent in combat now. That can be especially damaging for a fighter when a more exciting alternative exists. In this case, the alternative is a barking Brazilian madman with dynamite in his fists.Silva is a more marketable option in some respects, with KO power that generates highlight reels and fan enthusiasm. Sterling wouldn't have accepted another dangerous opponent if he believed a title shot was in the bag. Beating Vallejos is important, but making a statement matters just as much.
Vallejos has his own ideas about Saturday's fight. The 24-year-old Argentine believes he can stifle Sterling's wrestling attacks long enough to knock him out. Sterling, whose grappling has frustrated some of the UFC's best fighters, isn't enthralled by that assessment. "If that's what he really thinks and believes, then he hasn't watched many of my fights," Sterling said. "So if that's his path to victory, as I said before, good luck. It's going to be a long night for this guy. If anything, I can make it a short one for him. So, let me get the takedown early and send you on your way home. Nice first-class ticket back home to Argentina."Even an impressive victory won't secure Sterling's immediate future. Volkanovski has expressed interest in finishing his career with a lightweight superfight against Justin Gaethje. Should Volkanovski stay put, it's possible that UFC matchmakers have already decided on Silva as the next title challenger behind closed doors. Sterling could find himself waiting or having to win again regardless of this weekend's result.
How long he's willing to pursue another title is difficult to answer. Sterling has spent almost his entire UFC career fighting ranked opponents, an unusually demanding schedule that has continued into his late 30s. Vallejos is the same age Sterling was when he signed with the promotion, and represents another generation of ambitious young fighters hoping to build their reputations at the old guard's expense."That's a hard question, man," Sterling said when asked how much longer he'd pursue a featherweight title shot. "I'm just taking it one fight at a time. See how my body does, see how I perform when I step in there with these guys. Again, these guys are so much younger than me. They're hungry. They want what I have, what I've been able to achieve. They want to make their names off of me. I understand because I was that young guy once before."I'm preparing to be the best version of myself. I go out there and do what I'm doing in the training room. It should be a beautiful night for the team, and I'll be dancing my way into a title shot opportunity."

title: 49ers lose shot at breaking NFL record for most miles traveled due to Week 11 travel detour en route to Mexico - CBS Sports
description: The 49ers are taking a detour in Week 11 that's going to cost them the NFL record for most miles traveled
body:
The 49ers are taking a detour in Week 11 that's going to cost them the NFL record for most miles traveled
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 20, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:51 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        With a trip to Australia in Week 1 and a trip to Mexico City in Week 11, the expectation before the season started was that the 49ers were going to break the NFL record for most miles traveled this season, but that's actually not going to happen due to a travel detour that the team is taking this week. After beating the Cowboys in Week 10, the 49ers didn't fly home to California. Instead, they took a flight to Colorado, where they spent the week getting acclimated to the high altitude in Mexico City, which sits at an elevation of 7,350 feet. The 49ers' decision to head to Colorado will reduce the total number of miles the team travels this year. If the 49ers had flown home after their game against the Cowboys, they would have traveled a total of 2,876 miles round trip. After that, their round-trip flight to Mexico City would have covered 3,702 miles for a two-week total of 6,578 miles. However, since the 49ers didn't fly home after playing the Cowboys, that will lead to a drastic change in their mileage total. Here's what their Week 10 to Week 11 travel will look like (the 49ers fly out of San Jose): 
San Jose to Dallas (1,438 miles)Dallas to Colorado Springs (592)Colorado Springs to Mexico City (1,376)Mexico City to San Jose (1,851)Total for all four: 5,257 milesThe decision to practice in Colorado this week will cut their total travel by 1,321 miles this year, trimming their season total from 38,105 miles to 36,784. At that number, they won't set the NFL's mileage record. The Los Angeles Chargers set the record for most travel miles last season when they flew 37,086 miles, and that record will stand for at least another year thanks to the 49ers' decision to take a pit stop in Colorado before heading to Mexico City in Week 11. 
That being said, the 49ers will be setting one NFL record when they take the field on Sunday: They'll become the first team in NFL history to play two international games in two different countries in non-consecutive weeks. The Vikings played in Ireland and England last season, but that came in back-to-back weeks. The 49ers' two international trips are coming 10 weeks apart.
